title: ORM Leak Exploitation via Filter/Search Injection

technique.summary: Exploit ORM search/filter capabilities by injecting ORM-specific query operators through API parameters. Many frameworks pass filter parameters directly to ORM query builders, enabling operators like $ne, $gt, __startswith, and nested where clauses to extract data the API was not intended to expose.
steps: Identify API endpoints that accept filter/search parameters (e.g., ?field=value, JSON body filters)
Test for Sequelize operators: field[$ne]=null, field[$gt]=, field[$in][]=value
Test for Django ORM lookups: field__startswith=a, field__regex=^a, field__icontains=test
Test for TypeORM FindOptions: {"where":{"field":{"$not":null}}} or field=!null
Confirm data leak by extracting values character-by-character via $regex or __startswith
Chain with blind extraction: iterate through charset, use boolean response differences to reconstruct secret values

payloads.notes: Sequelize — returns all records where field is not null (bypasses intended equality filter)
Sequelize — returns all records (greater-than empty string matches everything)
Sequelize/Mongoose — regex filter for blind character-by-character extraction
Django ORM lookup injection — test if field starts with 'a', iterate charset for blind extraction
Prisma nested where filter — blind extraction via startsWith
Sequelize $in operator — test for specific values in set

bypassTechniques: URL-encode operators: %24ne, %24gt, %24regex to bypass WAF or input sanitization
Use array syntax: field[$ne]= instead of JSON operator format
Nested JSON objects: {"field":{"$ne":null}} in request body instead of query string
Try both query string and JSON body — different parsing paths may have different sanitization
Double-encode operators for frameworks that decode twice: %2524ne
Use ORM-specific aliases: Sequelize Op.ne vs $ne, Django __exact vs =
